Container.Name: reauth-bot
Container.Overview: Standalone Schwab trusted-device re-consent bot (repo: github.com/sdr-ventures/reauth-bot). Self-contained image; on a ~96h cadence it drives a target service's login flow inside a persistent trusted-device profile (skips 2FA) so the Schwab 7-day consent refreshes itself. This template targets Tape; LOGIN_URL/TOKEN_URL have no default and must be set at creation. REQUIRES a one-time interactive trusted-device seed: set SEED_MODE=1 + SEED_VNC_PASSWORD, Apply, complete the consent over noVNC (http://CONTAINER-IP:6080/vnc.html), then clear SEED_MODE and Apply. The trusted-device cookie MUST persist across updates (Profile volume). Alerting follows the fleet's shared ops-alerting convention: set DEPLOY_ENV and mount the shared alerting config read-only at /kw_shared (see github.com/sdr-ventures/kw-common/blob/main/docs/alerting-setup.md); each run reports OK/ERROR to both email and ntfy. Unlike most of the fleet this container is FAIL-OPEN on a bad alerting config — it degrades every channel to unconfigured rather than refusing to start, so a missing mount or a broken DEPLOY_ENV never stops the reauth loop itself. See the reauth-bot repo README.
Container.Description: Standalone Schwab trusted-device re-consent bot (github.com/sdr-ventures/reauth-bot). Self-contained image; UI-deployed; one-time seed via SEED_MODE. This template targets Tape.

Config.Name: Profile
Config.Description: Trusted-device browser profile + /profile/shots debug captures. REQUIRED - an absolute path on a POOL. It MUST survive updates and reboots: losing it forces the manual interactive re-seed.

Config.Name: SCHWAB_USER
Config.Description: Schwab login id (drives the trusted-device browser login)

Config.Name: LOGIN_URL
Config.Description: The service's login endpoint the bot navigates to start consent — a credential-less browser route, e.g. https://tape.your-domain.example/v1/public/login (NOT /v1/admin/login, which now requires an admin credential a browser cannot send)

Config.Name: TOKEN_URL
Config.Description: Set at creation. The target service's token-status endpoint the bot reads (HTTP GET, sending TAPE_CLIENT_ID/TAPE_CLIENT_SECRET as X-Client-Id/X-Client-Secret) to confirm consent advanced. Use the service's DIRECT/internal URL (its container IP:port) — NOT a public CDN host (Cloudflare 403s non-browser requests). Format: http://SERVICE-IP:PORT/v1/auth/token (the auth-scoped path; /v1/admin/token now requires admin)

Config.Name: TAPE_CLIENT_ID
Config.Description: Client id (X-Client-Id) the bot presents on the TOKEN_URL read. Register a client dedicated to the bot holding ONLY the auth scope via the service's /v1/admin/clients (client_id=reauth-bot, scopes=auth) so it can be rotated or revoked on its own. Set together with TAPE_CLIENT_SECRET — this tool has no other reason to run.

Config.Name: TAPE_CLIENT_SECRET
Config.Description: Client secret (X-Client-Secret) for TAPE_CLIENT_ID — the one-time value returned when the client was registered. Set together with TAPE_CLIENT_ID.

Config.Name: Shared alerting config
Config.Description: READ-ONLY mount of the shared config directory. Set the host path to the directory holding configs/alerting.env (EMAIL_TO, EMAIL_FROM, SMTP_HOST, SMTP_PORT, SMTP_USER, SMTP_PASSWORD, NTFY_URL_PROD/NTFY_URL_DEV, and optionally NTFY_URL_REAUTH_BOT for this service's own topic). Without it every alert channel is unconfigured. The container-side target is HARDCODED in the image to match this mapping's Target below — do not change the Target.

Config.Name: DEPLOY_ENV
Config.Description: REQUIRED - type prod or dev. Picks which ntfy topic from the shared file this container publishes to (NTFY_URL_PROD or NTFY_URL_DEV) absent its own NTFY_URL_REAUTH_BOT override, and which keys the shared file must carry. DELIBERATELY BLANK by default: a wrong guess here silently pages the wrong topic. Case does not matter. Unlike most of the fleet, leaving this blank does NOT stop the container from starting — it only leaves alerting unconfigured.

Config.Name: ALERT_SELFTEST
Config.Description: Set to 1 and Apply to send ONE test notification on the next start (proves email + ntfy without waiting for a reauth cycle), then clear it back to blank. Blank = off.

Config.Name: REAUTH_INTERVAL_HOURS
Config.Description: Refresh cadence in hours (~4d; ≥1 retry of margin before the 7-day Schwab wall). The bot also SKIPS the reauth on startup if the consent is already fresh, so a restart never adds a redundant one.

Config.Name: REAUTH_NOW
Config.Description: Set to 1 and Apply to force ONE reauth on the next start, regardless of how fresh the consent is — the way to confirm a changed Schwab password works now instead of days later. Clear it once the run succeeds, or every restart spends a reauth. Blank = off. Do NOT use REAUTH_INTERVAL_HOURS=0 for this: a successful run then sleeps zero hours and the bot reauths in a tight loop.

Config.Name: REAUTH_RETRY_HOURS
Config.Description: Retry interval after a failed run, in hours

Config.Name: SEED_MODE
Config.Description: Set to 1 ONLY for the one-time interactive seed (headed browser over noVNC on :6080); blank = headless steady state

Config.Name: SEED_VNC_PASSWORD
Config.Description: Required when SEED_MODE=1 — VNC password gating noVNC (the seed is a live brokerage login on br0). Blank refuses to start in seed mode.

Config.Name: REAUTH_SEED_HOLD_SECONDS
Config.Description: How long (s) the seed keeps the headed browser open for you to log in + approve 2FA. Raise if a slow SMS 2FA risks closing it mid-login.

Config.Name: Seed noVNC
Config.Description: noVNC port, used ONLY during the seed (SEED_MODE=1). Reach it at http://SERVER-OR-CONTAINER-IP:6080/vnc.html (on bridge it's the host IP; on br0 the container IP).
